text:
Talia Benson: trying to close out pilot readiness owners for Dedicated burst option. can folks reply w/ DRI + “done by” for your slice? aiming for a crisp go/no-go checklist for next week’s readiness review.

Talia Benson: draft checklist (please add / correct):
- Control plane config schema + migrations shipped (ENG-4822)
- Policy evaluation deterministic + cached (ENG-4823)
- Routing fallback semantics implemented + tested (ENG-4824)
- Fleet burst pools provisioned + labeled + excluded from baseline guarantees (ENG-4825)
- Telemetry: admit/deny + usage + saturation metrics + cardinality controls (ENG-4826)
- Dashboards + alerts + paging policy (ENG-4827)
- Guardrails: cooldown/backoff + global circuit breaker (ENG-4828)
- Billing hooks: shadow metering tags baseline vs burst + reconciliation report (ENG-4830)
- Load/perf canary scenario for spike traffic + pass/fail gates (ENG-4831)
- Rollout tooling: feature flags by tenant/region + rollback/disable command (ENG-4832)
- Security review complete (ENG-4833)
- Customer docs + config examples + retry guidance (ENG-4829)
- Runbook: burst pool saturation + mitigations + escalation path

Connor O'Brien: +1. also want a single “pilot-ready” definition we can paste into the ENG-4821 epic.

Lauren Bishop: PM side: I’ll own pilot customer selection + beta terms + external comms. Will sync w/ Markus/Miguel but I’ll be DRI. Target: shortlist + enablement checklist by Fri.

Ethan Park: Control plane schema/migrations: DRI me. Current status: schema in review, migrations staged behind feature flag.
Ethan Park: ETA: merge + deploy to staging by Tue; prod roll by Thu (assuming no surprises). Need Jordan/Mina to confirm fields they need (policy/routing).

Jordan Lee: policy engine DRI me. We have deterministic eval in place, but still tuning cache invalidation + deny reason codes.
Jordan Lee: ETA: code complete by Wed, integration test w/ routing by Thu.
Jordan Lee: ask: we need a canonical list of deny reasons that are safe to surface (internal vs external). Mina/Sean can you weigh in?

Mina Haddad: routing DRI me. Fallback semantics doc is “baseline -> burst -> deny (429) OR fallback model/region (503?)” still not fully locked.
Mina Haddad: I propose for pilot: baseline attempt first, then burst if eligible, if burst denied due to limit/saturation then return 429 + `x-redwood-burst-deny-reason` (coarse), and only do cross-region/model fallback if explicitly enabled by tenant policy.
Mina Haddad: ETA: integrate policy result in route selection by Fri, tests by Mon.

Sean Gallagher: re: 429 vs 503: +1 to 429 for “policy/limit denied” (client can back off); 503 for “system unhealthy” cases. but please keep reason codes constrained.
Sean Gallagher: SRE readiness (alerts/runbook/paging): DRI me, with Rafael as backup.
Sean Gallagher: ETA: dashboards drafted by Wed, alert thresholds + paging policy by Fri, runbook updates by Mon.
Sean Gallagher: we also need a “kill switch” playbook: who can disable burst per-tenant + globally and how fast.

Rafael Mendes: can take rollout/disable procedures + oncall comms as DRI. We’ll want `rbctl burst disable --tenant <id> --region <r>` documented + permissioned.
Rafael Mendes: ETA: first pass runbook section by Fri.

Vanessa Ortiz: Fleet/pools: DRI me. we have initial pool topology proposal ready; provisioning depends on quota confirmation but labels/isolation are straightforward.
Vanessa Ortiz: ETA: pool labels + exclusion checks in place by Thu. provisioning in 2 regions first (us-east-1, eu-west-1) by early next week.
Vanessa Ortiz: question: do we want dedicated-only clusters for burst pools in pilot or shared cluster w/ strict partitions? (we can do either, but timeline differs)

Peter Holtz: from routing/SRE embed POV: shared cluster is fine if we have clear admission gates and pool saturation alarms. dedicated-only clusters reduce blast radius but slower.
Peter Holtz: suggest pilot on shared cluster + strict pool labels + circuit breaker, then revisit for GA.

Keiko Yamamoto: guardrails (cooldowns/backoff/circuit breaker) DRI me. I’ll pair w/ Vanessa for fleet integration.
Keiko Yamamoto: ETA: cooldown params + circuit breaker thresholds in config by Fri; defaults safe + overridable per tenant.
Keiko Yamamoto: also want a “cooldown active” metric to make it obvious why burst is getting denied.

Logan Wright: telemetry DRI me. metrics set mostly agreed but we need to lock dimensions to avoid cardinality blowups.
Logan Wright: ETA: emit counters/gauges (admit/deny, tokens, reqs, saturation, cooldown_active) by Thu; dashboards can consume after.
Logan Wright: Nadia/Cole can you confirm what billing needs to attribute baseline vs burst? want to reuse tags.

Nadia Rahman: for shadow metering we need a reliable “usage_class=burst|baseline” tag in the usage record, plus pool_id + region.
Nadia Rahman: DRI me for metering pipeline changes, with Cole.
Nadia Rahman: ETA: tagging + reconciliation report by next Tue.

Cole Summers: +1. I’ll own quota/billing hooks integration points w/ control plane (permissioning + limits). Let’s keep it shadow-only for pilot.

Elliot Price: docs DRI me (w/ Kira). We need final error semantics + customer-visible config schema examples.
Elliot Price: ETA: draft customer docs by Mon, final edits once Mina/Jordan confirm response codes + headers.

Kira Thompson: I can do the Dedicated Console wording + “how to set limits” examples. also include a section “what happens when burst is denied” w/ retry guidance.

Connor O'Brien: capturing owners in ENG-4821 now. if anyone sees missing items, reply.

Talia Benson: thx all. open items to resolve in this thread:
1) Fleet topology for pilot (shared cluster vs separate) -> tentative: shared cluster w/ strict pool labels + circuit breaker
2) Customer-facing deny semantics (429 vs 503) + safe headers
3) Kill switch: command + permissions + runbook location

Vanessa Ortiz: confirm (1) ok w/ me. shared cluster pilot, but we must document: burst pools are isolated capacity + never counted towards baseline dedicated guarantees.

Mina Haddad: for (2) I’ll write up a 1-pager in the routing spec and post here. leaning:
- 429 = not eligible / limit exceeded / cooldown / pool saturated
- 503 = system error / upstream unhealthy
and header `x-redwood-burst: attempted|admitted|denied` + `x-redwood-burst-deny-reason: limit|cooldown|saturation|ineligible` (no tenant/pool identifiers)

Sean Gallagher: works. pls also ensure we log full internal reason + pool_id in traces (not exposed to customer). and we need alerting keyed off deny rate + saturation.

Rafael Mendes: (3) I’ll partner w/ Ethan on permissions. we should define who can run the disable command (SRE oncall + incident commander) and audit log it.

Ethan Park: ack on audit logging. we can emit an admin action log entry when burst is toggled. I’ll add to control plane tasks.

Talia Benson: awesome. I’ll send calendar for readiness review + paste updated checklist/DRIs into the ENG-4821 epic. please keep updating statuses there so we don’t lose track. :thumbsup:
